citation: Alken, P., Thébault, E., Beggan, C.D. et al. (2021) International Geomagnetic Reference Field: the thirteenth generation. Earth Planets Space 73, 49. doi:10.1186/s40623-020-01288-x
description: The International Geomagnetic Reference Field is a standard mathematical description of the Earth's main magnetic field, expressed as spherical harmonic Gauss coefficients, with definitive (DGRF) models for past epochs and a predictive secular variation. It is produced by the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy through a task force that combines candidate models from institutes using satellite, observatory and survey data; the 14th generation coefficients were finalised in November 2024. Coverage is global and the model runs from 1900 to the present in five-year epochs, with older generations kept for reprocessing legacy surveys. NOAA NCEI provides access to the coefficients as a text file and spreadsheet, the Geomag 7.0 program for Windows and Linux, a Fortran program from the British Geological Survey, Python code on GitHub, and online calculators. The Geomag software is public domain and free. Caveats: the IGRF represents only the core field, not crustal anomalies or the rapid external variations that drive space weather, and predictive values degrade towards the end of each five-year period. In infrastructure simulation it gives the background field and magnetic coordinates needed for geomagnetically induced current modelling, satellite attitude and navigation corrections, and compass-based systems; related records are INTERMAGNET, SuperMAG and OMNI.
